# Free source-facet affine neutrality forces the simplex centroid

This is a bounded rigidity lemma linking an actual critical-circuit
response to its geometric source. It is not an OC proof. In particular
it assumes canonical simplex cap directions and neutral responses to
independent signed affine velocities on the source facets. The point is
that neutrality can identify an already solved class instead of producing
an incorrectly asserted neutral contact simplification.

## 1. A sufficient actual freedom condition

Let P be finite and lattice-complete in its affine hull. Let positive
convex bodies K_z be the actual sections at P of their convex hull. For
each q in P consider the polytope of representations

    q=sum_(z!=q) a_z z, a_z>=0, sum a_z=1.

It may be empty. It has finitely many extreme points. Every anchored
Minkowski inclusion is implied by the inclusions for these extreme
representations: for each continuous normal, the sum of supports is
linear in a, hence attains its maximum at an extreme point. A
representation also using q reduces to one not using q by moving its
q-term to the other side of each support inequality.

Fix p in P. Suppose every extreme anchored inclusion with p as target
or with a_p>0 as input is STRICT, meaning its compact Minkowski sum is
contained in int K_q. Finitely many such inclusions have a common positive
support margin epsilon. Every other extreme inclusion is unchanged when
only K_p varies. If d_H(K_p',K_p)<epsilon/2, the support at p changes by
less than epsilon/2. Each affected input support sum changes by at most
that amount, as does an affected target support. Input and target cannot
both be p in these representations. Thus all inclusions remain valid.
The hull of the changed family still has exactly its prescribed fibers.

If K_p is a simplex, this permits arbitrary independent small signed
affine outward velocities on each of its facets. Indeed, with one facet
initially n.x<=h, |n|=1, replace it by

    n.x<=h+t psi(x),

where psi is affine, and leave the other facets fixed. For both signs of
sufficiently small t the defining normals still describe a bounded
positive simplex: invertible vertex-intersection matrices and strict
opposite-vertex margins persist. Its vertices and therefore the simplex
are Hausdorff continuous. The initial outward normal velocity on that
facet is psi, and the others have zero velocity except on their null
edges. Simultaneous finite facet tilts work in the same way. In d=1
these are independent endpoint motions with counting boundary measure.

This is a sufficient condition, not a claim that an arbitrary attained
extremizer has strict anchored inclusions.

## 2. Exact source rigidity theorem

Let K=conv(v_0,...,v_d), d>=1, be one actual source fiber, and let
lambda_0,...,lambda_d be its affine barycentric coordinates. Suppose a
regular critical circuit through an interior source y has own-fiber cuts

    H_j intersect K={x in K: lambda_j(x)>=q_j},
    q_j=lambda_j(y)>0, sum_j q_j=1, 0<=j<=d.          (1)

Regularity here excludes positive-area cap/body facet coincidences on
EVERY measured fiber. The caps may have arbitrary integer tilts; no
assumption on their statuses in the other fibers is made. Normalize their
continuous normals to unit length, so proper coarea is Euclidean section
area, and use circuit coefficients rho_j for those same normalized normals.
Let theta_j>0,
sum theta_j=1, be their actual equal-budget response weights, obtained
from circuit coefficients rho_j and full proper coarea S_j by

    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_h rho_h/S_h).

Put W=sum_j theta_j 1_Hj on the source boundary. Let beta>0. Assume the
normalized circuit response is zero for every independent signed affine
velocity on every source facet. By the ordinary cap first variation and
the regular circuit quantile formula this says precisely

    integral_(F_i) psi(x)(W(x)-beta) dH_(d-1)(x)=0
                   for all affine psi and every i.           (2)

Then beta=Gamma_d. If d>=2, also y=g_K and theta_j=1/(d+1).
The statement about y is not asserted when d=1.

Proof for d>=2. Let A_i be the positive area of F_i and let
g_i=(1/d)sum_(j!=i)v_j. For j!=i, the cap on F_i is exactly the
homothetic simplex q_j v_j+(1-q_j)F_i. It therefore has relative area
(1-q_j)^(d-1) and centroid q_j v_j+(1-q_j)g_i. The j=i cap is empty.
Taking psi=1 in (2) gives

    sum_(j!=i) a_j=beta,
    a_j=theta_j(1-q_j)^(d-1).                       (3)

Subtracting any two rows makes all a_j equal. Each row has d terms,
so a_j=beta/d>0. Taking the coordinate affine tests in (2) and using
(3) yields

    sum_(j!=i) q_j(v_j-g_i)=0.                      (4)

Affine independence of the d vertices of F_i implies q_j is constant
over j!=i: the coefficients of these vertices in (4) are
q_j-(1/d)sum_(h!=i)q_h, have sum zero, and must all vanish. Because
d>=2, for any two indices one can omit a third; hence all q_j agree.
Equation(1) gives q_j=1/(d+1), so y=g_K. Then (3) and sum theta=1 give
theta_j=1/(d+1) and

    beta=(d/(d+1))*(d/(d+1))^(d-1)=Gamma_d.

For d=1, each source endpoint is captured by exactly its own vertex
cap, so (2) with constants gives theta_0=theta_1=beta. Their sum is one,
yielding beta=1/2=Gamma_1. No endpoint first-moment equation supplies
the missing equality of q_0 and q_1.

## 3. Conditional application to a minimum with one witness

Suppose an actual local minimum has a single selected circuit covering
every deepest base plane, with persistent slack covers for the other
bases. Suppose the regularity, canonical source-simplex, and signed
source freedom hypotheses above hold. Each of these finite signed
variations gives an upper comparison for maximum normalized depth.
Local minimality makes its first response nonnegative. The response is
linear and both signs are feasible, so it must be zero. Thus(2) holds,
and the theorem gives beta=Gamma_d. Such a configuration cannot be a
counterexample with beta<Gamma_d/2^n.

For multiple witnesses, local minimality applies to the maximum of their
responses. It does NOT make any one response neutral in every direction.
The preceding argument must not be applied separately to each witness.
Nor may supporting coincidences be assigned arbitrary fixed theta_j.

## 4. A companion status constraint from independent translations

Keep one regular minimal positive circuit with UNIT continuous normals u_j,
positive coefficients rho_j and one-dimensional positive kernel
sum rho_j u_j=0. Let S_j be its total proper coarea. Suppose its normalized
response is neutral under every translation of one independently movable
fiber K_z. Let S_j(z)>=0 be that cap's proper section area in K_z.
The fiber mass does not change, while the cap derivative under translation
t is S_j(z)u_j.t by fiberwise Gauss--Green. Neutrality therefore gives

    sum_j theta_j S_j(z)u_j=0.

The kernel assumption and theta_j proportional to rho_j/S_j imply that
S_j(z)/S_j is independent of j. Thus either EVERY cap has positive proper
coarea in this fiber, or NONE does. A mix of proper and strictly full or
empty statuses is impossible under these precise neutrality assumptions.
Regularity excludes supporting-facet branches from this calculation.
This is a necessary status condition, not a claim that all fibers are
independently movable or that neutrality is automatic for several witnesses.
